Second development release of 0.19.0: PRTG monitoring as a full integration (status, sensors with gauges on device and VM pages, alarms, acknowledgements both ways, maintenance pauses, adoption and inventory drift), application groups that put a server's whole software stack on it in one step and hand it to Ansible, an Application map under Maps, a Compliance page built for triage, the software version each device really runs with a Versions view, a fuller end-of-life card per application, and the first security fix of the 0.19 line.

> [!CAUTION]
> **This is a development release. It is not stable and it contains bugs.** Do not run it in production or on data you can't restore. Take a backup before upgrading a test install, and expect behaviour to change before 0.19.0. If you run into a problem, please [submit a bug report](https://github.com/danbyte-net/danbyte/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) - every report helps get 0.19.0 right.

> [!NOTE]
> **Behaviour changes:**
> - **Notification channel credentials are write-only.** `GET /api/monitoring/channels/` no longer returns a Slack, Teams, Discord or webhook channel's `url` or a PagerDuty `routing_key`; it answers `url_set` and `routing_key_set` instead, like the Telegram `bot_token_set`. Sending a value in `config` still sets it. The upgrade moves stored values into the encrypted store; the services must be restarted straight after the migration, which the upgrader does, or those channels cannot send in between.
> - **Compliance opens on Overview.** `/compliance` now starts on the new Overview tab; the Violations and Rules tabs keep their URLs and filters.
> - **The Applications list opens in tree order**, a parent followed by its children, instead of alphabetically.
> - **Software versions carry a source.** Existing versions are marked `virtualization` when an integration set them and `manual` otherwise. An automatic source never overwrites a manual or imported value.
> - **Site roles gain the new types.** Existing site viewer and editor roles are upgraded to cover application groups and their assignments, PRTG links, sensors, changes, pins and host facts.
> - **A new timer.** `danbyte-extmon-sync.timer` drives the shared external-monitor beat that PRTG runs on; `make install-services` links and enables it on upgrade. Zabbix keeps its own timer.
> - **Zabbix runs on a shared layer.** The Zabbix integration moved onto `monitoring/external/` (severity map, matching, review queue, adoption, maintenance, acknowledgement hooks) with no schema or behaviour change.

### Applications

- #436 - **Application groups.** DCIM → Devices → Application groups holds named sets of applications such as *RDS* or *SCADA*, each member with an optional starting version. Assign a group from a device's or VM's Software tab, from the group's Hosts tab or in the device and VM forms, and the host gets one install per member; unassigning removes the installs it created and keeps any that were edited. A member added to a group later lands on every host it is assigned to. Adding a parent application offers to include its children, which join as members of their own in tree order.
- #436 - **Groups in the Ansible inventory.** `/api/inventory/ansible/` lists each host's `application_groups` and `applications` (name, slug, version, group), and every assigned group becomes an inventory group `app_group_<slug>`, so a play can target `hosts: app_group_rds` or loop over the host's applications.
- #436 - **End of life on the application page.** The card names the source and product with links out, lists every cycle the installs run with its status, end date, latest version and the installs on it (each count opens the Installed on tab filtered to that cycle), says plainly when the product is not in the catalog or none of the versions match, and offers Change product, Remove and, for admins, Refresh now.
- #436 - **Hierarchy.** The application page's Overview shows the path to the root as crumbs and the children three levels deep with their install counts; the Applications list opens in tree order with each child marked under its parent; Installed on filters by cycle and shows a *manual* chip where the cycle was set by hand.
- #436 - **Backlinks.** The End of life badge on a device's or VM's Software tab and the End date of a software row on the Lifecycle page open the application's card; the Lifecycle page gains an Application column and filter, and the application's install count opens it filtered.
- #436 - **Software on device and VM pages.** The Software tab shows its count, the Overview gets a Software card with the first installs, their versions and time left, and installs can be added from the application's Installed on tab as well. The VM Disks and device Support contracts tables now match the other Overview cards.
- #436 - **Groups tab.** An application's page lists the groups it belongs to.

### PRTG monitoring

- **Connection.** Settings → Integrations gains **PRTG monitoring**; the `/prtg` page holds the connection (URL, API key stored encrypted and write-only, read interval, TLS check) with **Test connection** reporting the PRTG version, probe and sensor counts and whether API v2 answers. The classic API is read with the key as `apitoken`; API v2 is probed with a bearer token.
- **Status like Zabbix.** Every read interval Danbyte reads the sensor table, matches PRTG devices to its own devices and VMs (stored link, a `danbyte-<id>` tag, address, DNS name, exact name; two candidates at one level go to the review queue as "Needs a decision"), rolls the sensors up per object through an editable **state map** (Up, Warning, Unusual, Down, Down (Partial), Down (Acknowledged) → Danbyte's states; paused, unknown, no probe and not licensed stay unknown), and feeds a `prtg` check kind that can be narrowed by sensor type or tag. A PRTG column and `?prtg=` filter on the device and VM lists; a push endpoint for PRTG's "Execute HTTP Action" that triggers a re-read of one device.
- **Sensors on device and VM pages.** A **Sensors** tab with a status strip, one card per sensor (last value, last check, uptime, PRTG's message when not up, a link into PRTG) and a panel per sensor with one card per channel: an arc gauge with warning and error bands for numbers, a segmented state bar for lookups, "No value" where PRTG has none, a sparkline and 1h/24h/7d history read from PRTG on demand and cached for one interval. The Monitoring tab shows a PRTG summary row. Channels can be **pinned to the Overview**.
- **PRTG overview.** `/prtg` shows all sensors with state counts, an **Alarms** tab (down and degraded sensors with message, since when and acknowledged state) and a **Sensors** tab with facets and search.
- **Dashboards.** Two widgets: **Sensor** (a device or VM, a sensor and a channel as gauge, lookup bar, value or sparkline) and **Sensor alarms**.
- **Two-way.** Acknowledging a Danbyte alert on a `prtg` check acknowledges the PRTG sensors behind it, and a sensor acknowledged in PRTG acknowledges Danbyte's alert, without echoing. Confirmed maintenance windows can pause the linked PRTG devices and resume them after (off by default; devices paused by hand are never touched). PRTG devices nothing matches can be **adopted** into Danbyte through adoption rules and defaults (off by default). PRTG's system information can feed the inventory drift inbox below a direct SNMP poll (off by default).
- **Shared gauges.** The gauge, lookup bar and sparkline are shared primitives for Danbyte's own checks to reuse.

### Application map

- #163 - **Maps → Applications.** A new map on the topology engine with two views. *Tree* lays the application hierarchy out in rows with the hosts underneath; *Flows* draws every flow between its ends with protocol and ports on the line, arrowheads by direction and colour by status. Filters for application, status, protocol and host, a search, a legend, detail panels on click, and PNG, SVG, PDF and draw.io export.
- #163 - **Legible lines.** Each application has a stable colour, shown as a bar on its card and on its host lines; host lines run in a channel per application and meet each host at its own point; no line crosses a card it does not connect to, in either view; hovering or selecting an application or host focuses its lines and fades the rest; a Hosts option offers Off, Row or Under applications.
- #163 - **The Diagram tab** on an application's page is now the embedded map in the page's own theme, with a link to the full map.

### Compliance

- **Overview tab.** The Compliance page opens on a row of counts (rules, passing, with violations, objects in violation, open per severity), a card per rule showing OK or how many objects fail it, worst first, with search, Hide passing and grouping by severity or object type, and a Top offenders table.
- **Violations built for triage.** Facets for state, severity, rule, object type, site and tags; group by rule with collapsible headers; select rows to Acknowledge, Snooze until a date or Reopen with a note, each change logged and journaled; every filter in the URL.
- **Triage is its own permission.** Acknowledging, snoozing and reopening need `compliancetriage.change`, separate from editing rules; the built-in Administrator and Operator roles have it and Read-only can view the triage log. An acknowledgement applies to the current occurrence: when an evaluation finds the object passing it is cleared and logged, and a later failure is open again; a snooze keeps its date.
- **Rules and the rule page** show the severity and current result; the rule page's Results tab has a Triage button into the filtered Violations.
- **API.** `GET /api/compliance/summary/` returns the counts and per-rule results in one call; `/api/compliance/evaluate/` gains facets and the site, tag, state and multi-rule filters; `POST /api/compliance/triage/` acknowledges, snoozes or reopens up to 1,000 pairs.

### Lifecycle

- #451 - **Where a version comes from.** Devices and VMs record the source of their software version (manual, SNMP, virtualization, Oxidized, import) with the time an integration last set it, shown next to the version on the Overview. A value someone typed is never overwritten by an integration.
- #451 - **Versions read from SNMP.** The version is extracted from `sysDescr` for IOS, IOS-XE, NX-OS, Junos and EOS, or by a per-platform version pattern on the platform form; `manage.py extract_software_versions` re-reads stored facts, and saving a new pattern queues that.
- #451 - **Versions view.** Lifecycle gains a Versions view: version by platform with device and VM counts, on-target state and sources, filterable by site, platform and role, each count opening the filtered list; `GET /api/lifecycle/versions/` behind it, and `?software_version=` and `?software_version_source=` on the device and VM lists.

### Fixed

- **Notification channel credentials were readable by every viewer.** Webhook URLs and PagerDuty routing keys came back in the channel API to any user who could view channels, including the built-in Read-only role, and a failed test send could echo the webhook path. They are now stored encrypted beside the Telegram token, never returned, and the error is masked.
